subject: Animation
title: Ernesto de la Cruz: The Charming Fraud
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ernesto de la Cruz: The Charming Fraud.

hook.text: Ernesto de la Cruz in Coco is worshipped as Mexico's greatest musician — beloved by the living and the dead.

buildup.text: Miguel idolizes Ernesto, believing he is his great-great-grandfather who chose music over family.

discovery.text: Ernesto murdered his real songwriting partner Héctor and stole every song that made him famous.

twist.text: He is charming in death as in life. His villainy works because everyone — character and audience — wants to love him.

climax.text: Ernesto showed that the most effective animated villain is someone the audience genuinely admires before the reveal.

punchline.text: The greatest animated frauds are the ones the audience also falls for.

quiz.question: What makes Ernesto de la Cruz an effective villain in Coco?
options: He has supernatural powers in the Land of the Dead
The audience genuinely admires him before discovering he murdered his partner and stole his songs
He is the most physically intimidating Pixar villain

details.summary: Ernesto de la Cruz from Coco is a beloved musician revealed to have murdered his friend and stolen his songs. His twist villain status hits harder because Miguel — and the audience — genuinely admired him.
details.whyItMatters: Ernesto shows how charisma and fame can mask terrible deeds, a theme with real-world resonance. The betrayal feels personal because the audience invested emotional trust alongside Miguel.
takeaways: Ernesto's villainy is revealed gradually through narrative twists
His charm makes the betrayal feel personal to both Miguel and viewers
He embodies how fame can conceal a person's true character

faq.question: Why does Ernesto's villain reveal work so effectively?
faq.answer: Unlike Hans in Frozen, Coco plants clues throughout. Ernesto's songs don't match his personality, and small inconsistencies accumulate. The reveal recontextualizes everything the audience has seen, rewarding careful viewing.

faq.question: What real-world theme does Ernesto de la Cruz represent?
faq.answer: He represents how society idolizes celebrities without knowing their true character. His story asks whether we can separate art from the artist, and what happens when our heroes turn out to be fundamentally corrupt.
